task: land a meeting time with another person through a scheduling tool (Calendly, Doodle, Microsoft Bookings): open the invite link — or set up the event/poll and get it answered — compare availability, pick a slot, confirm; complete when the meeting-confirmed screen, or the poll's agreed final time, is on screen with the event details. Either side of the handshake belongs as long as the recording reaches a confirmed time. Surface pinned: a scheduling tool on the web. Variants: emailing back and forth about times, plain calendar-event creation with no counterparty, and configuring availability settings without a resulting booking do not belong.

tree.label: Schedule a meeting with others
tree.note: do 1. 2, 3, 4 in the order the tool's wizard dictates - Doodle and Outlook describe first (eZyb, W0fS), Google Calendar sets the rules first and takes the description on page two (VKIQ); 5.1 comes before 3 in the mail family, because the poll pane stays disabled until someone is on the To line and the availability icons need those names (VxrV, KbIz). then 5. 6 happens on the other side of the link - nine keepers cross over, always by simulating the invitee. 7 on poll routes only: booking routes commit at 6.5.4, and when2meet stops at the heatmap with no close at all (ythO). 8 interleaves from the first committed change - holds are checked minutes after sending (VxrV), rule edits are checked by refreshing the public page mid-setup (6Pzf). 9 when the offer needs editing and re-sharing, or taking down.

children.label: Get into the scheduling tool
children.note: 1.1 and 1.2 on web arrivals from search (udxi, X48l, 6Yg3); 1.3 once, on the desktop add-in (KbIz). 1.4 as the account state demands - most keepers arrive signed in, one goes guest, one registers from nothing, and Doodle lets creation start first and injects the wall mid-flow (MVu8, udxi). 1.5 whenever a nag interrupts. then 1.6 and 1.7; 1.8 where a first run offers it (VKIQ).

questions.question: Which search result should you click to access the official Doodle scheduling tool?
questions.why: The first organic result displays the URL 'https://doodle.com', confirming it is the legitimate platform for scheduling meetings.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that the agent navigated to the authentic and secure scheduling service rather than a deceptive link.

questions.question: Is the scheduling tool actually free to use, as promised in the search results?
questions.why: The search result at 00:14 promises a free tool, which is confirmed at 02:18 when the poll is created without a payment prompt.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance of a free service if the agent selects a tool that eventually requires payment.

questions.question: Should you accept all cookies or review the privacy purposes?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to control which third-party partners can store and access your personal data.

questions.question: Have you verified that the FindTime add-in is installed and published by Microsoft?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the security of personally confirming the authenticity and correct installation of the scheduling add-in.

children.label: Handle the account
children.note: 1.4.1 decides the route: guest skips the rest (M5A9); a fresh account runs 1.4.2 then 1.4.3 (MVu8); a returning one runs 1.4.3 alone. Doodle lets 1.6 and 1.7 happen before any of it (udxi).

questions.question: Should you log in or proceed as a guest?
questions.why: The screen displays 'Sign up' and 'Log in' options, prompting a choice between the speed of guest access and the tracking benefits of a registered account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to decide if the long-term tracking benefits of an account outweigh the immediate convenience of proceeding as a guest.

questions.question: Should you log in or get started?
questions.why: The top right navigation offers 'Log In' and 'Get started', requiring a choice based on whether an account already exists.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to use an existing scheduling profile or create a new one.

questions.question: Should you register manually with an email and password, or use a single sign-on option like Google or Microsoft?
questions.why: The screen presents a choice between filling out standard text fields or using third-party accounts like Google, Microsoft, or Facebook to create your profile.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over your account security and privacy preferences, as the agent might link a third-party account instead of keeping this tool's login separate.

questions.question: How do I complete the email verification?
questions.why: The screen showed an email from Doodle containing a 'Verify email' button needed to confirm the account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to personally review their inbox and ensure the verification link is legitimate before clicking.

questions.question: Which Google account should you use to sign in, and do you accept the data sharing terms?
questions.why: The screen displays multiple Google accounts to choose from and notes that continuing will share your name, email, and profile picture with Doodle.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over which specific personal or business identity is linked to the scheduling tool and its associated data sharing permissions.

questions.question: Should you connect your calendar to the scheduling tool or skip for now?
questions.why: The screen offers a 14-day premium trial to sync your calendar, which affects whether your existing appointments are automatically checked.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to grant the platform access to their personal calendar data or stick to the free manual version.

questions.question: Should you connect your Zoom account to set up the meeting location, or dismiss the pop-up?
questions.why: The screen shows a prompt to finish setting up the meeting location by connecting a Zoom account, which dictates how participants will meet.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If the agent dismisses this prompt without asking, you lose the ability to have Zoom links automatically attached to your scheduling link.

questions.question: Where do you click to start creating a scheduling poll?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to initiate the scheduling poll in a brand new email or as a reply to an existing conversation.

questions.question: What type of event do you want to create?
questions.why: The screen offers distinct options for a group meeting, a 1:1 meeting, or a survey, which dictates the format and functionality of the scheduling poll.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might select the wrong event format, such as setting up a 1:1 meeting when you actually need to coordinate multiple attendees.

questions.question: Should this new meeting type be public or private?
questions.why: The screen offers 'Public' meetings that appear on your booking page and 'Private' meetings that are only visible to those with the link.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might expose a meeting type publicly that you intended to keep restricted to specific invitees.

questions.question: Should you create the older style of appointment slots?

questions.question: What title should you give the group poll?

questions.question: Did you actually type a title into the field before proceeding?
questions.why: The claim states 'Example' was typed into the Title field, but the screen at 1:03 shows the field is still empty.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to successfully create the event without errors if the agent fails to input required fields like the title.

questions.question: What should you name the meeting?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the opportunity to personally set a clear, context-specific title that establishes the right tone for the attendees.

questions.question: What instructions or policies should you include in the event description?

questions.why: The screen provides an optional description field to give participants more context about the meeting.

questions.question: Where do you want the meeting to take place?

children.label: Offer the times
children.note: 3.1 before the tool opens, where it happens at all; 3.2 and 3.3 wherever the pane puts them. then 3.4 on booking-page routes (VKIQ, LDkn, 6Pzf) or 3.5 on poll and one-off routes (everyone else) - no keeper runs both. re-entered after publish through 9.2 (udxi).

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to control the granularity of their schedule, potentially leading to awkward gaps if slots are offered too frequently or inflexibility if they are too sparse.

questions.why: The screen shows a duration dropdown and a 'Work hours' checkbox that prevents times like 12:00 AM from being offered when checked.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to dictate the exact meeting length and protect your off-hours from being scheduled.

questions.why: Creating a calendar event for a task like the 'Revision to YT Script' automatically removes that time slot from your scheduling page so others cannot book it.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to prioritize their own private work sessions by blocking out specific times before opening their calendar to others.

questions.question: What should the duration, date, and time constraints be for the meeting you want to propose?
questions.why: The screen displayed default settings for the meeting's duration, date, and working hours that needed to be tailored to the specific context of the meeting.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to apply their personal judgment on appropriate meeting lengths and time zone considerations for specific attendees.

questions.question: What duration should I set for the meeting?
questions.why: The screen requires selecting a meeting duration from options like 60, 90, or 120 minutes to properly size the proposed time slots.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might select a duration that is either too short to cover the agenda or unnecessarily long for the participants.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the ability to strategically offer time slots that best fit your personal energy levels or unwritten preferences.

questions.question: Do you want this booking schedule to run indefinitely, or should it have a specific end date?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might keep the default four-hour minimum notice, exposing you to unexpected last-minute meetings without enough time to prepare.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent might not account for personal, unrecorded commitments that affect your actual availability on that specific day.

questions.question: What buffer time is currently set for after the event?

questions.why: The screen provides options to select which calendars to check for availability and to customize the color of the appointment schedule.

questions.why: The booking form allows you to add custom required fields, which determines the specific context collected from attendees before the meeting.
